memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh and said to them, "You have done all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded, and you have obeyed me in everything I commanded. For a long time now — to this very day — you have not deserted your fellow Israelites but have carried out the mission the Lord your God gave you." — Josh 22:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The war was over, and the land was won. Now Joshua calls the eastern tribes — Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh — to commend them. These tribes had received their inheritance on the far side of the Jordan, yet they had crossed over with their brothers and fought alongside them for years until every tribe was settled. They could have stayed home; instead they kept their word to the end.

Joshua's praise is warm and specific: "you have not deserted your fellow Israelites." That is a rare and beautiful thing — people who finish what they promised, who do not slip away when their own needs are met but stay until the whole task is done.

This is the kind of faithfulness God honours. It is easy to start well; it is much harder to remain steady "for a long time now — to this very day." Yet Scripture calls us to exactly this kind of endurance, not growing weary in doing good (Gal 6:9).

Above all, this points us to Christ, the one who was faithful to the very end, who did not abandon His mission even at the cross (Heb 3:6). Because He endured, He now gives us the grace to endure too. Ask Him today for the steadiness to finish what you have begun.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there commitments you have started but not yet finished?
2. What helps you stay faithful "for a long time," not just at the start?
3. How does Christ's own faithfulness encourage you today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for those who stay faithful to the end. Make me steady and dependable, and help me not to grow weary in doing good. Amen.
